label: Food Insecure Population
source: IPC Sep 23, 2026 (Reuters) / WFP / OCHA / UN Jul 2026
contestNote: UPDATED Sep 23, 2026 (IPC/Reuters): a new IPC report projects 5.4 million Somalis (~26% of the analyzed population) will face IPC Phase 3 Crisis-level hunger or worse between October and December 2026, including 1.5 million in Emergency-level hunger, with roughly 26,000 displaced people in Baidoa (Bay Region, ~5% of the city's displaced population) at real risk of famine-level starvation if anticipated El Nino flooding is worse than expected and aid funding stays insufficient — the first year-end famine-risk projection of the crisis for Baidoa specifically. Only ~70,400 people/month (~1.3% of those in need) are currently reached by food assistance; 1.92M children aged 6mo-5yr will require acute malnutrition treatment through June 2027 (433,000 severe). Somalia last saw famine in 2011 (~250,000 deaths) and narrowly avoided it in 2017 and 2022. Prior figure (6.5M, Jul 14) reflected a different, broader caseload measure; UN Humanitarian Coordinator George Conway's Jul 14 'real and credible risk of famine' finding for Burhakaba District remains the district-level baseline this Baidoa warning builds on. HRP funding level not re-confirmed since Jul 14 (15.2%).
delta: NEW Sep 23, 2026: IPC projects Baidoa famine risk for ~26,000 IDPs by year-end; 5.4M projected Crisis+ Oct-Dec
deltaNote: Reuters (Sep 23, 2026): IPC warns of possible famine conditions in Baidoa by year-end absent sufficient aid and if El Nino flooding is worse than projected. This is a forward-looking Oct-Dec projection distinct from the Jul 14 current-caseload figure, so no direct numeric delta is shown.

label: AUSSOM Authorized Strength
source: UNSC Resolution 2809 / AU / ChimpReports Jul 1, 2026 / Reuters Sep 18, 2026
delta: US grants UN 12-month drawdown window (from Jan 2027) instead of immediate Dec 31, 2026 cutoff
deltaNote: In a July 1, 2026 letter to the African Union, the US said it will not support UNSOS — AUSSOM's logistics backbone (fuel, medevac, food, engineering, COE reimbursement) — beyond Dec 31, 2026, and will oppose any UNSC renewal including UNSOS support. Cites Somalia's failure to take ownership of security despite ~$2B in UNSOS support plus $1.6B bilateral aid over a decade. AU Commission convened an emergency meeting; a senior African diplomat called the decision 'irreversible.' UPDATED Aug 25-26, 2026 (Radio Dalsan / WardheerNews): the drawdown moved from planning to execution — at least 10 civilian AU-UN Information Support Team staff received termination notices effective Sep 10, and UNSOS began auctioning vehicles, generators, medical supplies and other equipment. UPDATED Sep 18, 2026 (Reuters/US News, CNBC Africa): the US told the UN in a diplomatic note it is willing to support a 12-month drawdown followed by liquidation of UNSOS, starting January 2027, rather than the earlier all-at-once Dec 31, 2026 cutoff; final timelines to be set during December UNSC deliberations. Analyst Samira Gaid warned UNSOS's shutdown could still trigger AUSSOM's collapse; Prof. Afyare Elmi called AUSSOM 'a key pillar of Somalia's state,' with its loss risking 'a real risk of state fragmentation.' Defence Minister Fiqi countered publicly on Sep 20 that Al-Shabaab 'cannot capture even a single village' even if AUSSOM leaves. UNTMIS separately remains on track to complete transition to a standard UN country team by Oct 31, 2026. Roughly 11,862 uniformed personnel still depend on UNSOS for supply and shelter. Separately, funding and logistical hurdles have delayed deployment of Egyptian troop reinforcements to AUSSOM. UPDATED Sep 19-21, 2026 (Middle East Eye, Caasimada): a new fault line emerged when Uganda — AUSSOM's largest troop contributor at roughly 6,500 personnel (about 4,500 AU-mandated plus 2,000 bilateral) — suspended all defence cooperation with Turkey. Uganda cited Ankara's refusal to extradite a government critic, but regional sources said the real driver is Somali pressure on Uganda to wind down its deployment (worth an estimated $60-72M/year to Kampala) as Turkish-trained Somali forces expand; neither government has confirmed the Somalia link on the record. UPDATED Sep 24, 2026 (Dawan Africa, Arab News): President Mohamud met UN Secretary-General Guterres in New York during the UNGA's 81st session high-level week to discuss continued support for AUSSOM; Guterres 'reaffirmed the United Nations' commitment to Somalia's key national priorities' but no new funding commitment was announced. In his General Assembly address the same day, Mohamud called for 'predictable, sustainable support for Somalia's security transition, including adequate financing for an African Union mission in Somalia.' AUSSOM/UNSOS mandates still expire Dec 31, 2026; final drawdown timelines remain pending UNSC deliberations in December.

label: Piracy Hostages (Simultaneous, 2026)
source: Arab News / Dawan Africa / Marine Insight Sep 25-26, 2026 / IMO
contestNote: UPDATED Sep 25, 2026: the Puntland Maritime Police Force and Puntland Navy freed the US-sanctioned tanker Sibu 1 (Seamull, 20 crew) off Mudug's coast in a 48-hour armed operation — 1 pirate killed, several wounded, 15-41+ suspects detained depending on the source, all crew safe. It is the first armed recovery (rather than ransom release) of a 2026 piracy case. Reporting on the rescue also surfaced MT Asana — a Tanzanian-flagged tanker with ~20 crew seized off Yemen around Jul 17, 2026 and taken to Puntland's Bari region — which this tracker had not separately counted; it remains held alongside Honour 25 (17 crew, £3M ransom demand) and MT Eureka (12 crew, $10M demand), all reportedly relocated toward Hobyo, Galmudug. The Cameroon-flagged Lutuf is no longer mentioned as held in the Sep 25-26 roundups (status unconfirmed — may have been resolved without being reported to this tracker). Net: 17 (Honour 25) + 12 (Eureka) + 20 (Asana) = ~49 hostages across 3 vessels; no comprehensive IMO/EU NAVFOR re-count published.
delta: Sibu 1 (20 crew) rescued by Puntland forces Sep 25; MT Asana (~20 crew) added to count as previously untracked
deltaNote: The headline hostage count moves down primarily because Sibu 1's 20 crew were freed; the vessel count also drops from 4 to 3 currently held. MT Asana's addition is a correction of an existing gap in this tracker's coverage, not a new hijacking.
